newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Dev Fin Auth/Palos Cmmty Hosp raised by S&P.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Dev Fin Auth/Palos Cmmty Hosp raised by S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's today has raised its rating on Illinois Development Finance Authority's $76.5 million variable rate demand bonds series 1994A, issued for St George Corp. doing business as Palos Community Hospital, to double-A'/A-1'-plus-c from double-A'-minus/A-1'-plus-c.

Additionally, Standard & Poor's has withdrawn its double-A'-minus rating on Illinois Health Facility Authority's bonds series 1985A that have been redeemed, which also were issued for Palos Community Hospital.

The long-term rating upgrade reflects the 337-staffed bed Palos Community Hospital's excellent management, very strong patient utilization and financial performance, and abundant liquidity. The short-term rating continues to reflect a stand by purchase agreement (SBPA) issued by Credit Suisse covering the purchase price for tendered bonds. The "c" subscript indicates that the SBPA will automatically terminate if the long-term rating assigned to the hospital is reduced below triple-B'-minus by Standard & Poor's.

Palos Community Hospital's favorable location in an affluent suburb south of Chicago enables this facility to flourish as a result of continued strong management. Admissions increased 2% to 16,204 in the fiscal year ended Dec. 31,1996. Occupancy based on staffed beds is 62.3%. In addition, most outpatient and ancillary services showed similar growth. The hospital's payor mix is very favorable with only 30% of revenues derived from Medicare and 1% from Medicaid. The bulk of revenues are derived from numerous managed care contracts. While Palos Community Hospital is a stand alone hospital and has no immediate affiliation plans with other providers, its very strong overall profile has enabled it to participate in all managed care plans offered in the service area.

Financial performance is outstanding with excess margins recorded in each of the past five years in excess of 13%. In fiscal 1996 Palos Community Hospital recorded a 18% excess margin beating the prior year's 17.5% results. Leverage is modest with a 27% debt to capitalization ratio and the hospital has no immediate additional debt plans. Cash and board designated funds total in excess of $270 million providing 678 days cash on hand with only $91.5 million of long-term debt outstanding.
The outlook reflects Standard & Poor's belief that the hospital will continue to exhibit very strong patient utilization and financial performance with limited needs for additional debt.
